result: The authors defined the interactome of the human mitochondrial ribosome using SILAC-based quantitative mass spectrometry of mL62FLAG purifications. They identified all mt-ribosome components, mtDNA/RNA maintenance proteins, ribosome biogenesis factors, known OXPHOS assembly factors (COX20, COA1), and two uncharacterized proteins (TMEM223 and SMIM4) as ribosome-associated factors.
evaluation: Claims C32-C38 are well-supported by multiple lines of evidence including sucrose gradient fractionation (Figure 1A), SILAC mass spectrometry with four biological replicates (Figure 1B-C, Supplementary files), and validation by co-immunoprecipitation/western blotting (Figure 1D). The identification of TMEM223 and SMIM4 as novel interactors is confirmed by both mass spec and immunoblotting. The suggestion that the ribosome acts as a platform for OXPHOS assembly (C90) is a reasonable inference supported by the data and prior literature.

result: TMEM223 is an integral inner mitochondrial membrane protein with both termini facing the matrix that acts as an early assembly factor for cytochrome c oxidase. Loss of TMEM223 reduces COX1 synthesis to ~60%, decreases complex IV levels and activity to ~60%, and causes compensatory increase in complex III to ~165%. TMEM223 interacts with early MITRAC complexes (C12ORF62/MITRAC12) but not late complexes (MITRAC7/CMC1).
evaluation: Claims C39-C44 establish TMEM223 topology through standard biochemical approaches (protease protection, carbonate extraction; Figure 2A-C). The functional role (C4-C6, C45-C52) is supported by CRISPR knockout validation, steady-state protein analysis (Figure 2D), BN-PAGE quantification with n=3 replicates (Figure 2E), activity assays (Figure 3A), and [35S]methionine labeling showing specific COX1 synthesis defect (Figure 3B-C). Co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 3D-G) demonstrate selective interaction with early MITRAC components. The data converge to support TMEM223 as an early complex IV assembly factor.

result: SMIM4 is an integral inner mitochondrial membrane protein with one transmembrane domain and C-terminus facing the intermembrane space. SMIM4 interacts with mt-ribosome components, early complex III assembly factors (UQCC1, UQCC2, C12ORF73), and mitochondrial quality control machinery (mAAA-protease, iAAA-protease, prohibitins, SLP2), but not with late complex III assembly factors (UQCC3, RIESKE).
evaluation: Claims C56-C60 establish SMIM4 topology using standard methods (sequence prediction, STED microscopy, protease protection, carbonate extraction; Figure 4A-D). The interactome (C61-C66) is defined by SILAC mass spectrometry with four biological replicates (Figure 4E, Supplementary file 2) and validated by western blotting (Figure 4F). The selective enrichment of early but not late complex III factors is consistent across both mass spec and immunoblotting, supporting SMIM4's role in early complex III assembly.

result: C12ORF73 is an integral inner mitochondrial membrane protein with C-terminus exposed to the intermembrane space. C12ORF73 co-isolates with early complex III assembly factors UQCC1 and UQCC2, but not with late factors UQCC3 or RIESKE. Reciprocally, RIESKE immunoprecipitation recovers UQCC3 but not C12ORF73, SMIM4, or UQCC1.
evaluation: Claims C67-C70 establish C12ORF73 localization through STED microscopy, carbonate extraction, and protease protection (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-C), consistent with prior work (Zhang et al., 2020). The selective interaction with early assembly factors (C71-C72) is demonstrated by co-immunoprecipitation experiments (Figure 5A, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D-E). The reciprocal immunoprecipitation with RIESKE provides strong evidence for the temporal separation of early and late assembly complexes.

result: SMIM4 and C12ORF73 function as interdependent early complex III assembly factors that interact with newly synthesized cytochrome b and form a complex with UQCC1 and UQCC2, but not UQCC3. Depletion of either SMIM4 or C12ORF73 reduces complex III levels to ~60%, impairs cell growth by ~50%, and causes accumulation of a CYTB-UQCC1-UQCC2 subcomplex.
evaluation: The functional interdependence (C73-C74, C99) is demonstrated by reciprocal knockdown experiments (Figure 5B). The interaction with newly synthesized CYTB (C7, C83) is shown by [35S]methionine labeling and immunoprecipitation (Figure 6D). Complex composition (C78-C82) is established by 2D BN-PAGE/SDS-PAGE (Figure 6A-C). Functional effects (C75-C77, C100-C101) are quantified by cell counting and BN-PAGE with n=3 replicates (Figure 5C-E). The accumulation of assembly intermediates upon C12ORF73 depletion (C84) provides direct evidence for the assembly defect (Figure 6E). Multiple complementary approaches converge to support the role of SMIM4/C12ORF73 in early complex III assembly.

result: The authors speculate that the increase in complex III in TMEM223 knockout cells may represent a compensatory stress response, that TMEM223 function may overlap with other assembly factors (C12ORF62, MITRAC12), and that residual SMIM4/C12ORF73 after knockdown or long complex III half-life may explain incomplete complex III loss.
evaluation: Claims C93-C95, C102-C103, and C105 are explicitly labeled as speculation by the authors. While the observations (complex III increase in TMEM223−/− cells, incomplete complex III loss after knockdown) are supported by data, the mechanistic explanations are hypothetical and require additional experiments to validate. These represent reasonable hypotheses for future investigation but are not experimentally demonstrated in the current work.

result: The authors provide extensive background on mitochondrial genome organization, OXPHOS assembly, complex IV (cytochrome c oxidase) assembly pathway including MITRAC complexes, and complex III (cytochrome c reductase) assembly pathway. They note that mechanisms coordinating mitochondrial translation with OXPHOS assembly remain poorly understood.
evaluation: Claims C1-C3, C9-C31, C86-C87, and C107 represent established knowledge in the field, supported by appropriate citations to prior literature. These claims provide necessary context for the study but do not represent novel findings. The characterization of the knowledge gaps (C86-C87) appropriately motivates the current work.

result: SMIM4 and C12ORF73 are not conserved in yeast, suggesting differences in complex III assembly between yeast and humans. Prior work on the zebrafish C12ORF73 homolog (BRAWNIN) suggested involvement in complex III assembly, with conflicting evidence about whether it acts before or during complex dimerization.
evaluation: Claim C110 is an inference based on sequence conservation analysis (established knowledge). Claims C111-C115 accurately summarize prior work on zebrafish BRAWNIN (Zhang et al., 2020), including the ambiguities in that study. The authors appropriately note that their human data (C116-C117) showing exclusive association with early factors differs from some zebrafish findings, highlighting species-specific differences in complex III assembly.

result: The authors conclude that TMEM223, SMIM4, and C12ORF73 support immediate assembly of newly synthesized proteins into assembly intermediates, linking translation to OXPHOS assembly.
evaluation: Claim C120 is a reasonable synthesis of the experimental findings. The interaction of these proteins with mt-ribosomes (Figure 1), their association with newly synthesized OXPHOS subunits (COX1 for TMEM223, CYTB for SMIM4/C12ORF73), and their presence in early assembly intermediates collectively support this conclusion. This represents an appropriate high-level interpretation of the data.
